key_insight: DAWG combines belief-propagation ensembles with graph sparsification to retain competitive quantum error-correction decoding performance while reducing reliance on post-processing.
engineering_relevance: Fewer post-processing calls and a smaller post-processing graph could reduce decoding latency tails and specialized-hardware resource requirements.
method: Run serial minimum-sum belief propagation on the full detector error model Tanner graph, then transfer posteriors to a sparsified graph.
Diversify ensemble members with distinct transfer matrices and randomized decoding schedules.
Apply order-0 Localized Statistics Decoding (LSD-0) as a post-processor.
evidence_signal: Numerical studies on bivariate bicycle codes and superdense color code circuits report performance similar to Relay BP and Vibe decoding with LSD-0, while calling the post-processor roughly ten times less often than Vibe at the same ensemble size.
watch_item: The abstract reports numerical results, not hardware measurements; real-time latency and resource savings still require implementation-level validation.
paper_title: Decoding with alternating weighted graph sparsification for quantum low-density parity-check codes
